_comment: MacroPad pendant key layout. Copy this file to your app config directory and edit
it there to customise the pendant without touching Python; the copy wins over this
shipped default. A malformed or unknown-action layout is rejected as a whole and
this default is used instead, with the reason logged -- the pendant never comes up
half-bound.
Keys are numbered 0-11, left to right then top to bottom:
'jog' keys are held while turning the encoder to jog that axis. 'modifiers' are
held while pressing one of their 'targets'. The same key may appear under several
modifiers with a different meaning in each. Every action needs two controls at once,
so a key bound nowhere simply does nothing.
Keep chord targets off the jog keys. A stroke of {jog key + modifier} would be
reachable by brushing a modifier while reaching for a jog key, and for something
like zeroing the work origin that is too easy an accident -- confirm-twice only
helps if you notice the prompt. With no overlap such a stroke spells nothing and
is completely inert.
Each target value is an action name from the list below. A few actions confirm by
default (press the key twice); override per binding with the long form:
"0": {"action": "zero_xy", "confirm": false}
Available actions:
margin          scan the loaded file's XY bounds (M495)
machine_home    go to machine home
safe_z          raise to safe Z
work_home       go to work origin
run_pause       start / pause / resume the job
stop            abort
spindle_toggle  spindle on/off
probe_z         probe Z (or open the probing screen)
probe_laser     toggle the wired probe's laser crosshair (M494)
level           auto-level the loaded file's area (M495)
probe_4th       probe the 4th-axis headstock, set work Z to the rotation centreline
zero_xy         set work X and Y zero here  (confirms)
zero_z          set work Z zero here        (confirms)
macro_1 .. macro_10   run the matching pendant macro from settings
